Hey y'all,

So many of us talk about societal collapse, invasion, etc. Now, most of us romanticize what'll happen when SHTF. However, I am under the conclusion that most of us, especially the urbanfolk, are not ready for anything to happen. If (when?) things go under, they're going to go under fast, and certain skills are going to be a necessity. I kind of want to start with some discussion on important skills.

Physical fitness is probably the most important skill to have under ours belts. I've spent the last year making myself fairly fit, bu it will take time for most of us. There is no need to become a fitness jock, but basic physical fitness will be outstandingly necessary. One of the most basic things is to make sure you can run. Without the ability to run a couple miles straight, you will be at a significant disadvantage. If you are not reasonably fit when the time comes, you won't be of much use to yourself nor your kin.

Fitness is more than just that, however. You'll need to be able to move. Many people can run or lift or whatever, but that matters little without endurance and the ability to put it to use. I do a lot of backpacking and hiking, and I think that the ability to walk 10-20 miles a day in possibly rough terrain is of extreme importance. One of the things I want us working on later is outdoor skills, but hiking can be a good introduction to both. It will also teach you to pack what you need, when you need it, thinking about long-term use of items.

Swimming is a further important goal. There are many adults that still do not know how to swim. Not only is this important to endurance and strength, but swimming is a learned skill. Knowing how to swim should be a basic, but important skill for all of us here. I implore everyone to work on their swimming abilities if possible, or learn how to swim if you don't know.

On top of all this, perhaps the single most important physical skill to learn for fitness is how to spend a day out in the heat without dying. This sounds stupid easy, but if you've never done it before, then it'll kill you (literally) when you have to spend a day outside. I live on the coastal part of South Carolina, where it's incredibly hot and humid. I work outside a lot, so this is an easy skill for me. However, I spend a lot of time teaching people who don't spend so much time outside, and you learn really quickly that almost nobody knows anything about hydration and heat. A basic, but incredibly important skill to learn is simply how to be outside and doing physical activity all day without dying from dehydration. With air conditioning and home comforts, almost everyone is a complete novice at even existing outside their home or a building for more than a day or two. Most people have no clue that they're so useless that they'll literally die within the first two days of existing outside the comforts of modern society. Y'all need to learn how to deal with hydration and dehydration, before you need it and it kills you in the most unromantic way to possibly go out.

If you plan on being important or useful when the time comes, basic skills such as these are things you MUST have, or else you will die, incredibly quickly. I implore everyone here to start off by learning these basic skills if they can, for they will be incredibly important.

I'm increasingly convinced that to change anything, we'll have to act on our own. This means directly taking action with our own hands when the time is right. However, we won't be able to take action if we're pacified by the comforting song of modern society. We must have physical skills if we wish to be able to take physical action. We should start acquiring these skills, now if possible. This is a lost philosophy: it requires patience to wait, but it also requires agency, where we act in certain ways now. The philosophy of agency is all but lost in Western society, which is why it is so stagnant. We cannot expect to vote our problems away like the useless progressives, and we cannot expect that some white knight will come down off his majestic steed to save our society when all is grim. We must go in with the expectations that we'll have to do things with our own hands. Part of this is actually being prepared, as conviction is worthless without the ability and skills to act on it. We'll need to be straight in purpose, sound of mind, and strong of body.

Practicing these skills will not only teach you skill, but creating a routine will help with discipline. That is another important skill for us to learn there.
